chunks: It is a mursal report with a broken sanad/isnad, because Jaʿfar ibn Bashir in the first narration said, “from the one who narrated it,” and this is unknown and must be discarded. And in the second narration he said, “from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinan or someone else,” so he transmitted it while doubting it; and that which is of this kind must not be acted upon. Even if the report were sound as it stands, it would be interpreted as referring to one who deliberately made himself junub and feared destruction for himself; then he performs tayammum, offers salat, and repeats the salat, although it would still be preferable for him to perform ghusl in every circumstance, as we shall mention later. And that which indicates that one who prayed with tayammum while junub is not required to repeat the salat is as follows.
What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of:
From Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Aban, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿid, from Ṣafwan, from al-ʿIṣ.
He said: I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a man who comes upon water while he is junub and had already prayed. He said: “He performs ghusl and does not repeat the salat.”

And Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah has narrated this hadith from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abi al-Khaṭṭab, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinan or someone else, from Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: the like of that. So the first thing concerning it is...

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: In a state of janabah requiring ghusl.
key_terms.خَبَرٌ مُرْسَلٌ: A report transmitted without a complete connected chain.
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ الصَّلَاةَ: He does not repeat the salat.
key_terms.مَجْهُولٌ: An unknown transmitter whose identity or reliability is not established.
key_terms.مُنْقَطِعُ الْإِسْنَادِ: Having a broken sanad/isnad in the chain of transmission.
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: He performs tayammum as a substitute purification.

ai.seo_question: If someone prayed with tayammum while junub and then found water, must the salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the weakness of a report due to irsal, disconnection in the sanad/isnad, and uncertainty in transmission, and therefore rejects acting upon it as legal proof. It then cites a stronger narration indicating that a person who prayed with tayammum while junub, and later found water, should perform ghusl but does not need to repeat the salat.
